Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like late 2017. The unemployment rate is 4.2% and the fed funds rate is about 1.16%, which fits October or November 2017. The 2-year yield at 1.58% and the 10-year at 2.37% also fit that period, as does a VIX near 10.5.

The payroll average of 91k over three months is weak, which matches the hurricane-distorted figures from September 2017. Headline CPI at 2.23% suggests September or October 2017. The 12-month equity return of 23.4% is consistent with October 2017.

The fed funds rate was 1.15% in October 2017 and 1.16% in November. Unemployment was 4.2% in September, 4.1% in October and 4.2% in November, though after revisions the values may differ. The 3-month payroll average is lowest around October 2017, when September was -33k, so the average of August, September and October would be about 91k at first release. With a 3-month change in the unemployment rate of -0.2, September 2017 (4.2% against 4.4% in June) fits too.

The 10-year yield was about 2.33% in September and 2.38% in October. The 2-year yield was 1.47% in September and 1.60% in October. Equity returns of +1.9% over the month are consistent with October, when the S&P rose 2.3%. Headline CPI in October was 2.0%, and in September it was 2.2%. The CPI of 2.23% points to September, but the market data fit October, so I'll go with October. The 2-year yield rose by 0.24 over three months, which is also consistent with October.
